question.problem: Calculate the circumference of the base of a cylinder given that its volume is $1\,536\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}$ and the ratio of its radius to its height is $\frac{1}{3}.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the fact that the ratio of the radius $r$ of the base to the height $h$ is $\frac{1}{3},$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{r}{h} & =\frac{1}{3} \\ h & =3r\end{aligned}
$$

The volume of a cylinder with radius $r$ and height $h$ is given by

$$
V=\pi {r}^{2}h.
$$

Substituting $V=1\,536\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}$ and $h=3r$ into the formula, we can find the value of $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {r}^{2}h \\ 1\,536\pi  & =\pi {r}^{2}(3r) \\ 1\,536 & =3{r}^{3} \\ {r}^{3} & =512 \\ r & =\sqrt[3]{512} \\ r & =8\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the formula for the circumference of the base is $C=2\pi r.$ So, we have

$$
C=16\pi \,\text{cm}.
$$
